Save the results object of a project version

Source: R/save_results.R
save_results.Rd

save_results() writes <results>/results.qs2, the one results object of the project version. It stops before it writes when check_results() finds a failure.

Usage

save_results(exclusions, estimates, tables, extra = list(), d = NULL)

Arguments

exclusions

A data.frame with the columns step, n_before, n_excluded and n_after, one row per exclusion step. Zero rows are allowed.

estimates

A data.frame of estimates.

tables

A named list of data.frames.

extra

A list of other results.

d

The analysis data, or NULL. pbn stores only its number of rows.

Value

Invisibly, the path of the results file.

Details

Call initialize_project() first. The results folder is the results element that initialize_project() returns. It is <home>/<version>_results/<scenario>/ for a scenario with 1 simulation, and <home>/<version>_results/<scenario>/sim_<kkkk>/ otherwise.

The object is a named list with exactly these top-level names: manifest, exclusions, estimates, tables and extra. pbn builds the manifest, a list with these elements:

  • pbn_version and r_version.

  • packages, a named character vector. The names are the attached and loaded packages that are not base packages, and the values are their versions. qs2 is always in the list, because it writes the file.

  • run_date, the date of the call as YYYY-MM-DD. It has no time, so two runs on one day with the same inputs and packages write the same bytes.

  • version, scenario, sim, sims and data_raw, from initialize_project(). data_raw is the data folder of the run.

  • For the scenario "real" only, data_md5, a named character vector with the md5 of each file directly in data_raw. initialize_project() computes it, so a file that the run writes after that call is not in the list.

  • For a fake scenario only, fake_md5, one string: the md5 of the code of fake_<scenario>(), without its source references. Two runs of one simulation on one day with the same code and packages then write the same bytes. This holds also when fake_<scenario>() stamps the time into a file. A change in a function that fake_<scenario>() calls does not change fake_md5.

  • n_rows_data, the number of rows of d, or NA when d is NULL.

See also

Other results: check_results(), read_results()

Examples

home <- file.path(tempdir(), "pbn_save_example")
dir.create(file.path(home, "v01_functions"), recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(file.path(home, "data"))
writeLines(
  "CFG <- list(scenarios = data.frame(scenario = 'real', sims = 1))",
  file.path(home, "v01_functions", "_cfg.R")
)
pbn::initialize_project("v01", home, file.path(home, "data"), env = new.env())
#> You are NOT sourcing into .GlobalEnv. All functions will be sourced into an environment that is returned from this function.
#> Sourcing all code inside /tmp/RtmpbNfz7k/pbn_save_example/v01_functions into 

pbn::save_results(
  exclusions = data.frame(
    step = "age 18 or more",
    n_before = 100,
    n_excluded = 4,
    n_after = 96
  ),
  estimates = data.frame(term = "x", estimate = 1.2),
  tables = list(counts = data.frame(grp = c("a", "b"), n = c(50, 46)))
)
names(pbn::read_results("v01", home = home))
#> [1] "manifest"   "exclusions" "estimates"  "tables"     "extra"     

unlink(home, recursive = TRUE)
